description: Initialize the mit-concam-pipeline project with UV, package layout, YAML config, and SLURM template
steps: Create the package with `uv init` and configure pyproject.toml with the correct name, entry points, and dependencies
Create the importable package layout: concam/ with __init__.py, cli.py, config.py, and placeholder submodules for ocr, adsb, projection, detection, aggregation, and storage
Write a YAML config for the MIT Green Building camera site covering: video path, ADS-B filter parameters (altitude threshold, radius), OCR region, detection thresholds, and site timezone
Write a SLURM submission script that accepts a date argument and runs `uv run concam run --date YYYY-MM-DD`
Verify `uv sync` completes cleanly and `uv run concam --help` prints usage

description: Implement the fixed-format timestamp OCR module with TrustButVerifyTracker integration
steps: Implement `concam.ocr.FixedFormatTimestampReader` with `read(frame) -> TimestampRead` using configurable slot positions and threshold values from OcrConfig (defaults derived from probing real frames)
Implement `TimestampRead` dataclass with fields: `parsed_dt`, `text`, `confidence`, `per_char_confidence`, `method`, `status`
Add EasyOCR as an optional fallback path, called only when confidence is below the configurable threshold, with `method='easyocr_fallback'`

Copy `TrustButVerifyTracker` from the reference codebase into `concam.ocr.tracker`, add attribution comment, and write property-based tests: perfect monotone sequences never re-anchor; one bad read among good reads produces a projected timestamp; a sustained offset triggers re-anchor
Write parser property tests: all valid canonical strings round-trip; impossible dates fail; invalid separators fail
Verify the module can be imported and `FixedFormatTimestampReader.read` returns a valid `TimestampRead` on a real frame crop

description: OCR visual spot-check: generate a grid of example OCR crops with parsed results for human review. This is important to understand that the key components work before all the paraphernalia is built
steps: Sample 30 frames uniformly from the April 8, 2026 daily timelapse and crop the timestamp region from each
Run `FixedFormatTimestampReader.read` on each crop and record the parsed timestamp, confidence, per-character confidence, and method (template vs easyocr_fallback)
Generate a single image grid (saved as PNG) showing each crop alongside its parsed text, confidence score, and method used, sorted by confidence ascending so the weakest reads appear first
Print a summary table to stdout: total frames, exact-parse rate, fallback rate, mean confidence, and the 5 lowest-confidence parsed results
User reviews the PNG grid and summary to confirm acceptable accuracy before proceeding to end-to-end CLI wiring

description: Use appropriate altitude in the ADS-B retireval. GNSS altitudes might not be as good as the barometric altitude that is being meausred by the airplanes
steps: Read the feder API documentation and determine the correct call to retrieve pings for a UTC date and bounding box
Check how the GNSS vs barometric altitudes compare and get a Hakiu agent to do a quick websearch to understand limitations of aircraft GNSS altitudes vs barometric altitde

determine the best way to use the barometric altitude. Store both in each ADS-B ping but use the barometric altitude + ISA atmoshpere or other to get the right altitude to use in the overlays if there is major discrepency between the GNSS and barometric altitudes

description: Implement the ADS-B loader using the feder package
steps: Read the feder API documentation and determine the correct call to retrieve pings for a UTC date and bounding box
Implement `concam.adsb.load_flights(date, config) -> list[Flight]` where each `Flight` carries callsign, a list of timestamped pings, and metadata
Filter pings to those within the configured horizontal radius and above the configured altitude threshold
Upsample each flight's ping sequence to one-second resolution by linear interpolation of latitude, longitude, and altitude
Write an integration test using a small checked-in fixture of real pings that verifies the correct number of pings and their timestamps after filtering and upsampling
Verify the loader returns a non-empty list of flights for April 9, 2026 using the local feder data store

description: Implement GPS-to-pixel projection using the MIT Green Building camera calibration
steps: Load the camera intrinsics and extrinsics from the calibration files in LAE_skycam/calibration/

Implement `concam.projection.project_ping(ping, calibration) -> PixelPoint | None` converting GPS (lat, lon, alt) to pixel (x, y) via ECEF -> ENU -> camera frame, applying OpenCV distortion correction
Return None for pings that project outside the image bounds
Implement `concam.projection.flight_path_vector(ping_a, ping_b, calibration) -> tuple[float, float]` returning the unit vector of the flight path in pixel space
Implement `concam.projection.oriented_roi(center_pixel, path_vector, config) -> Rect` returning the oriented bounding rectangle for detection
Write a test that projects a known GPS coordinate and verifies it falls within the expected image quadrant given the camera orientation

description: CRITICAL one of the key aspects of this project is to create the contrainal detection system. So this really needs to be built carefully. This is one that we should do with users involvement.
steps: Load 30 frame-flight pairs from April 9, 2026 timelapse where ADS-B data shows a flight overhead
Use the grill-me skill on the user to understand what is expected of hte detector modeule
Read the detect_prior_art.md
Create steps based on the outcome of the grill-me and add new tasks to this PRD.json

description: Implement the Hough+Canny contrail detector module
steps: Implement `concam.detection.detect(frame, roi, config) -> DetectionResult` where `DetectionResult` carries `score` (float 0-1), `pixel_line` (x1, y1, x2, y2 or None), and `method`
Apply Canny edge detection within the oriented ROI using parameters confirmed in the validation notebook
Apply Hough line transform and compute score as the peak accumulator value normalized to [0, 1]
Return the pixel line in full-frame coordinates (not ROI-local coordinates)
Write unit tests: a synthetic frame with a clear line in the ROI scores above 0.7; a blank frame scores below 0.1; corrupting one frame does not raise an exception

description: Implement per-day episode aggregation and DuckDB storage
steps: Implement `concam.aggregation.aggregate_episodes(frame_results) -> list[Episode]` that groups consecutive above-threshold (frame, flight) detections into episodes, recording onset time, end time, peak score, and the pixel line at peak score
Implement `concam.storage.Database` wrapping DuckDB with methods: `create_schema()`, `insert_episodes(episodes)`, `insert_labels(labels)`, `query(sql)`
Write the `contrail_episodes` table schema with all fields from the PRD; label fields are nullable
Write unit tests: three consecutive above-threshold frames merge into one episode; a gap of one frame splits into two episodes; peak score is the maximum over the episode
Write a schema test: inserting a valid episode row and querying it back returns identical values

description: Wire up the end-to-end batch CLI for a single date
steps: Implement `uv run concam run --date YYYY-MM-DD` that executes all stages in order: ocr, adsb, project, detect, aggregate, store
Each stage reads from and writes to a well-defined intermediate path under an output directory configurable via `--output-dir`
Add `--from-stage` flag to resume from a named checkpoint without re-running earlier stages
Add `--dry-run` flag that validates inputs and prints the execution plan without running any stage
Run the full pipeline on April 8, 2026 (daily timelapse available) and verify a non-empty DuckDB file is produced with at least one episode row
Verify `--from-stage detect` skips the ocr and adsb stages and reads their cached outputs

description: Implement the labeler bundle generator
steps: Implement `uv run concam bundle --date YYYY-MM-DD --labelers alice bob --overlap-fraction 0.2` that reads the DuckDB file for that date and produces one bundle directory per labeler
Each bundle contains: a JSON manifest with all episode metadata, ADS-B track pixels per frame, detection line segments, and assigned episode IDs; and the HTML labeler file
The JSON manifest references the video file by relative path; the video is not copied
The overlap set is selected deterministically (e.g., by sort order and modulo) so re-running the generator produces the same assignment
Verify that the two generated manifests together cover all episodes, with approximately 20% in both

description: Implement the browser-based labeler HTML/JS: video playback with canvas overlays
steps: Create a single self-contained HTML file that loads the JSON manifest from a relative path
Play the video using an HTML5 video element; synchronize a canvas overlay to the video's timeupdate event
Draw ADS-B flight tracks for all flights visible in the current frame; highlight auto-detected flights (score above threshold) in a distinct color
Draw the detected line segment for the current frame if one exists
Implement toggle controls: one toggle for ADS-B track overlays, one toggle for detected line segments
Verify the overlays are correctly positioned on a synthetic bundle with a short video and three known flight tracks

description: Implement the browser-based labeler HTML/JS: timeline navigation and label controls
steps: Add a timeline panel listing all flight episodes with callsign, score, and assigned label status
Clicking an episode marker seeks the video to the episode onset time
Episodes with auto-detected contrails are visually distinguished from undetected flights in the timeline
Add label controls per episode: three-way toggle (contrail / no_contrail / unsure), persistence slider (1-5), and free-text notes field
Autosave all label state to localStorage on every change
Restore previously saved labels from localStorage on page load
Add an export button that downloads the completed labels as a JSON file matching the schema expected by `concam storage insert_labels`
Display a clear human-readable error message if the video file is missing or the manifest fails to parse

description: ADS-B projection alignment check on real frames. The projection unit tests assert that landmarks land within ~80px of ground truth, which is fine for buildings on the ground but has never been verified for aircraft in the sky. A sign-flip or small extrinsics error would still pass landmark tests while putting overhead-flight overlays in the wrong quadrant — and if labelers can't trust the overlay, the labels are garbage regardless of detector quality.
steps: Select 5 flyovers from April 9 raw segments where ADS-B shows an aircraft crossing the camera FOV at high altitude with the aircraft visibly present in the video (use daylight segments so the aircraft itself is identifiable, not just its contrail)
For each flyover, project the ADS-B ping sequence using `concam.projection.project_pings` and render the pixel track on top of the raw video frames at 1-second intervals
For each frame, a human marks the pixel position of the visible aircraft and records the offset vector (track_pixel - aircraft_pixel)

Generate a summary: per-flyover median and max offset in pixels, and a scatter plot of offsets across the FOV to expose systematic distortion (e.g. radial error suggesting a bad distortion coefficient)
Go/no-go decision: if median offset > 100 px (roughly a small-plane-silhouette width at 4K), investigate calibration or extrinsics before proceeding to labeling
Record the offsets, summary, and decision as a markdown cell at the end of the notebook

description: Real-bundle browser smoke test: open a bundle produced from the April 8 daily timelapse in a browser and manually verify that overlays, label controls, and export all work end-to-end. Items 12 and 13 ship with only static HTML assertions; nobody has yet confirmed that the UI actually behaves correctly on a real video with thousands of flight tracks and hundreds of episodes.
steps: Run the full pipeline on April 8, 2026 (timelapse) to produce `pipeline.duckdb`, `projections.jsonl`, `detections.jsonl`, and `ocr.jsonl` under the output directory

Generate a bundle with `uv run concam bundle --date 2026-04-08 --labelers alice bob` and open `bundles/alice/labeler.html` in a browser served over http (file:// may block the fetch of manifest.json in some browsers)
Visually confirm: video plays, ADS-B tracks render on the canvas, detection lines render when auto-detected episodes are active, toggles show/hide each overlay layer
Click into 3 episodes (1 auto-detected, 1 undetected, 1 overlap); verify the video seeks to the episode onset and starts playing
Apply a label to each of the 3 episodes (one contrail, one no_contrail, one unsure), move the persistence slider, type notes, and reload the page — verify all state restores from localStorage
Click Export labels and verify the downloaded JSON has `{schema_version, date, labeler_id, exported_at, labels: [...]}` with 3 entries whose inner dicts match the `Database.insert_labels` contract
Record any visual glitches, alignment issues, or missing UX affordances as TODOs against items 12/13 so they can be patched before shipping bundles to real student labelers

description: Implement label ingestion from student JSON files into DuckDB
steps: Implement `uv run concam ingest-labels --labels alice_labels.json bob_labels.json --date YYYY-MM-DD` that reads completed label JSON files and populates the label fields in the DuckDB database
Validate each label JSON against the expected schema before writing; print a clear error for malformed files
Handle the overlap set correctly: if both labelers labeled the same episode, store both rows with distinct labeler_id values
Verify that after ingestion, a SQL query returns the correct label, persistence_rating, labeler_id, and label_timestamp for each ingested episode

description: Implement inter-rater agreement computation
steps: Implement a query or notebook cell that joins the two labelers' labels on the overlapping episode set
Compute percent agreement and Cohen's kappa on the three-class label (contrail / no_contrail / unsure)
Print a confusion matrix for the overlapping set
Verify the computation returns the correct kappa for a synthetic overlapping set where all labels agree (kappa=1) and where labels are random (kappa near 0)

description: End-to-end regression on April 8, 2026: full pipeline produces a stable labeled output
steps: Run `uv run concam run --date 2026-04-08` on the daily timelapse and record the number of episodes, the distribution of detector scores, and the number of flights processed
Re-run the pipeline with the same inputs and verify the episode count and scores are identical (determinism check)
Verify no stage raises an unhandled exception and the DuckDB file is valid and queryable after the run

Correctness spot-check: pick the top 5 episodes by peak_score and the 5 episodes nearest the detection threshold, visually inspect the underlying video frames, and record what fraction are true contrails. The purpose is to detect silent regressions that slip past the determinism check (e.g. a calibration or threshold drift that still produces the same episode count but flags wrong frames).
Record the full-day run metrics (episode count, flight count, detection rate, top/threshold episode correctness fractions) in `.ralph/progress.txt` so future regressions have a reference baseline

description: URGENT: Mask the burned-in OCR timestamp region so the detector never runs Canny/Hough on it. The April-8 spot-check surfaced BCS378 (13:13Z) where the rotated ROI landed on the 'WED 9:13:42' text and the bright glyph edges produced aligned Hough lines — a systematic false positive at every daytime ping that crosses the top strip. NRBR does not fix this (white text has NRBR≈0 like contrails), so it needs its own masking step. Also land a sun-elevation gate at the same time since downstream NRBR work only applies during daylight.
steps: Add `timestamp_exclusion_region` (or reuse `ocr.timestamp_region`) to the detection config: [y0, y1, x0, x1] in full-frame pixel coords, with a safety pad around the OCR box

In `concam.detection.detect`, zero out pixels in the exclusion region before Canny (or in `pipeline.stages.run_detect_stage`, skip candidates whose rotated polygon is fully inside the exclusion region)
Add a sun-elevation helper that returns sun_alt_deg for (timestamp, site_lat, site_lon) using a standard solar-position formula. Gate downstream NRBR-aware logic on sun_alt_deg > 0
Unit tests: a synthetic frame with a bright rectangle in the exclusion region + a contrail outside it → only the contrail scores; a contrail inside the exclusion region → score=0

Re-run April-8 regression and confirm BCS378, LOT16M (if it overlaps the strip), and any other top-strip episodes either drop out or drop to score=0. Diff episode count against the baseline 122 in `output/validation/regression/2026-04-08/metrics.json`

description: Detector honesty: re-run the April-8 detection sweep with `prev_frame` enabled so tuning is measured against the same input distribution the live pipeline runs against. Surfaced during the April-8 regression: the live pipeline passes `prev_frame` for temporal-diff pre-processing but the sweep / review-panels / NRBR spot-check all pass `prev_frame=None`. Re-running the spot-check without prev_frame produced top-5 BGR scores of 0.333–0.5 vs the stored 1.000, meaning the temporal-diff step is doing far more work than the sweep report implied and the production thresholds are tuned against a different signal than the sweep validated.
steps: Add a `--use-prev-frame` flag to `scripts/detection_validation_sweep.py` that, when set, decodes the frame immediately before each labeled candidate and passes it as `prev_frame` to `detect()`. Prior frames must come from the same video as the labeled candidate

Re-run the 2187-combo sweep on the April-8 labels with `--use-prev-frame` and compare AUC / Youden-J / top-10 combos against the prev_frame=None baseline already recorded in `output/validation/detection/2026-04-08/sweep_report.md`

If the top combo shifts, retune `DetectionConfig` defaults in `configs/mit_green_building.yaml` accordingly and re-run the April-8 regression to confirm episode count and score histogram move in the expected direction
Update `detection_review_panels.py` and `scripts/nrbr_spotcheck.py` to accept the same flag so panels reflect the live-pipeline input

description: Widen and lengthen the rotated detection ROI. Spot-check of April-8 top-5 episodes (MSR985, BEL1CP, AAL101, MSR988, DAL289) showed the current roi_along_px=120 / roi_cross_px=40 rectangle clips real contrail pixels on both ends and on the sides, so the detector only sees a fraction of the streak. The sweep validated these specific dimensions on a small label set; a rerun with larger dimensions (along the flight-path axis especially) should catch more aligned Hough lines without introducing FPs, since the mask still constrains Canny to the along-track strip.
steps: Extend the `scripts/detection_validation_sweep.py` grid to include `roi_along_px ∈ {120, 180, 240, 320}` and `roi_cross_px ∈ {40, 60, 80}`. That is a 12-cell sub-grid; keep the other axes frozen at the current best combo so the sweep stays tractable
Re-run the sweep on the April-8 labels (with `--use-prev-frame` from the honesty task if that landed first) and pick the (along, cross) pair that maximises AUC without regressing Youden-J
Update defaults in `configs/mit_green_building.yaml` and re-run the April-8 regression baseline. Expected outcome: higher score_mean / more top-bin detections, stable episode count
Visually re-render the spot-check panels at the new dimensions and confirm the rotated polygon contains the visible contrail streak end-to-end for top-5

description: Adaptive along-track ROI + physical-unit contrail length. Once a detection scores above threshold, grow the rotated rectangle progressively along the flight-path vector (both directions) and keep counting aligned long Hough lines until the length stops extending. Use the final along-track pixel length as the detected contrail extent, and convert to metres using aircraft alt_m + pinhole-ray geometry from the calibration. Persist `contrail_length_px` and `contrail_length_m` on each `DetectionResult` and each `Episode`; downstream, an episode's peak length is a natural persistence proxy (short-lived contrails are tens of metres, persistent cirrus-forming contrails stretch kilometres).
steps: Implement an adaptive-growth detector variant in `concam.detection` that, given a seed polygon + score above threshold, iteratively extends the along-track axis by `growth_step_px` until the aligned-long-line count stops increasing (or hits `roi_max_along_px`)

Add a `project_pixel_to_meters` helper in `concam.projection` that, given a pixel length along a known flight-path vector, the aircraft alt_m, and the camera calibration, returns the corresponding metres (slant-range × angular extent)
Extend `DetectionResult` with `contrail_length_px` and `contrail_length_m` fields; extend `Episode` with `peak_contrail_length_m`; extend the DuckDB schema and the bundle manifest accordingly
Unit tests: a synthetic 200-px streak at alt=10 km projects to the expected metres (~2 km ballpark); adaptive growth stops at the contrail's edge and does not drift into blue sky

Re-run the April-8 regression and add `peak_contrail_length_m` histogram to `metrics.json`. Spot-check: the top-5 peak_score=1.000 episodes should have non-trivial lengths, and very short lengths (<500 m) should cluster with the near-threshold marginal calls

description: LOW-PRIORITY exploratory: evaluate whether NRBR (normalized red-blue ratio) as a detector input channel improves AUC over BGR alone. The April-8 spot-check (`output/validation/regression/2026-04-08/nrbr_panels/`) showed contrails light up dramatically in NRBR for daytime frames — Rayleigh scattering physics working as intended — but under an apples-to-apples `detect()` call the BGR and NRBR scores came out numerically identical because Canny/Hough already captures the gradient structure in either representation. The real value of NRBR may be (a) looser detector thresholds that catch fainter contrails without new FPs, or (b) parallel scoring where the two channels vote. Whether either actually beats the current BGR tuning is an open question; only prioritise this if the timestamp-mask, prev_frame-honesty, ROI-widen, and adaptive-length tasks leave real AUC gains unreached.
steps: Add NRBR as a per-detection secondary score: run `detect()` on both BGR and NRBR-remap-to-uint8 and record both scores on each detection record
Re-run the April-8 sweep over the BGR-threshold and NRBR-threshold 2-D grid (gated on sun-elevation > 0). Compare AUC and Youden-J against the single-BGR baseline
If NRBR-only gives equal or better AUC at stricter-threshold, consider a dual-channel gate (score = max(bgr, nrbr) above threshold) vs sum-score (bgr + nrbr) and pick the one with better Youden-J
Update `concam.detection.DetectionResult` with `nrbr_score` and `Episode.peak_nrbr_score` only if the sweep justifies it; otherwise close this task as 'not worth the wire format churn'
Only run this AFTER the timestamp-mask task lands, since NRBR has the same timestamp-glyph FP as BGR and needs the mask too

description: Episode clip renderer: produce short annotated MP4 clips (±30 s around episode onset) with ADS-B track and detection line burned in. Motivated by the need to review detections outside the browser — JupyterHub file-proxy works for the HTML labeler but pre-rendered clips are portable (email, slide deck, any video player). Full-day annotated videos are too large; per-episode short clips are the right granularity.
steps: Implement `scripts/render_episode_clips.py --date YYYY-MM-DD [--top-n 10] [--output-dir output]` that reads `episodes.jsonl`, `projections.jsonl`, and `detections.jsonl` for the date

For each selected episode, seek the raw video to onset - 5 s, decode frames for onset - 5 s to end + 5 s (or 60 s max), and render each frame with: (a) ADS-B ping dot at the projected pixel for all flights in the frame, (b) the peak detection line segment drawn in the episode color (green = score > 0.5, yellow = marginal), (c) callsign + score + wall-clock burned in as text
Write each clip as a 720p H.264 MP4 using PyAV (already a dependency); downscale from 4K to 720p to keep file size under ~50 MB per clip
Add a `--episodes episode_id,episode_id,...` flag to render arbitrary episodes by ID, not just top-N
Verify the top-5 April-8 episodes render correctly: ADS-B dot tracks the visible contrail, detection line appears on frames where score > threshold

description: Interactive ROI dimension sliders in detection_inspect.ipynb: let the user drag roi_along_px and roi_cross_px sliders and immediately see the effect on the rotated polygon, gradient mask, Canny edges, and Hough lines — all without editing the YAML config. Once a good pair is found, a one-line code cell shows the config snippet to paste. This closes the feedback loop between visual inspection and threshold tuning.
steps: Add two IntSlider widgets to detection_inspect.ipynb: roi_along_px (range 60–1200, step 20, default=det_cfg.roi_along_px) and roi_cross_px (range 10–200, step 5, default=det_cfg.roi_cross_px)

Pass a temporary DetectionConfig override (copy det_cfg, overwrite roi_along_px/roi_cross_px from the sliders) into build_panels() so panels ②–⑥ reflect the slider values without touching the real config
Show the rotated polygon outline update live in panel ② as the along-track or cross-track dimension changes
Add a small read-only HTML cell below the sliders showing the YAML snippet: 'roi_along_px: N  roi_cross_px: M' so the user can copy the winner back to configs/mit_green_building.yaml
Verify that resetting sliders to defaults reproduces the same panels as the pre-slider notebook
